audits.cleanReason: 34 contrast-shaped or contrast-adjacent candidates went through the four-step procedure, and about 30 more plain negative statements were screened out before it: one-word answers, physical facts like 'gave no light at all', commands at L443/L445, and POV perception limits like 'She couldn't hear a word'. The narration contains no Not-X-Y fragment pivots, no source-swaps, no count resets, no mundane reveal chains and no minimizer pivots. Every pivot-shaped line is either dialogue, where the negated item is a real in-world claim that matters to the plot, or Sylvanas arguing with herself under condition 4, where the next sentence undercuts it. Dialogue cases: 'Damp doesn't stop at a street corner. This does.' (L105) overturns the physicians' diagnosis, and 'There'd been no brawl' (L121) admits the charge Havel actually filed was false. Self-argument cases: 'If he had seen her, he would not stand at the window like that ... Unless he had been taught to' (L333) and 'She had no better reason to doubt him than...' (L405). The one chained negation, 'no wagon, no doorway deep enough to stand in, no turning' (L299), builds toward no destination noun. It lists the cover she is missing, and that absence is what sends her onto the roof (condition 3). The KEEP rate is above the guide's 20% heuristic because the candidate list is deliberately inclusive. None of the candidates repeats the AI pivot rhythm. Each KEEP rationale is in the scratchpad.

audits.secondSweepP5P6: Re-read every sentence for inanimate or abstract subjects carrying verbs of agency, cognition, desire, combustion or behaviour. Roads and geography only take path-geometry verbs ('Hurdle Lane ran along the backs', 'It ran straight for a stretch, then bent left', 'The lane opened out'), which the guide treats as acceptable ('the road led'). The map and the papers get no cognition or revision verbs. In 'chalked on and rubbed out so many times that the streets had gone grey' the chalk literally greys the canvas, and 'the sheet curled up on itself' is paper physics. No abstract state settles into a body part. No inanimate subject collects a chain of human verbs across consecutive sentences. Body-part subjects were examined separately (L9, L29, L173, L297, L303, L329, L379). Each is an involuntary tremor, an impairment, a colour change, a state-describing absolute phrase, or a synecdoche forced by the POV ('Through the spokes she could see his boots'). None gives the body part knowledge or volition that the character owns. Actor-demotion check: in 'the staff took most of her weight' (L213) and 'The heel of the staff ground on the earth floor and the stool scraped back' (L433) the verbs are literal load and sound, and the actor is named in the same or the preceding sentence. In 'the lock went on from inside' (L421) the agent cannot be seen by the men reporting it.

findings.reason: The 'mark' family appears 16 times in this chapter, well past the 4+ density at which the guide says the word stops meaning anything specific. Fourteen of those are the literal plot noun: a yard's seal sign ('Fenner's mark', 'copied marks') or the tally-man's chalk mark. L243 is the only mental use (marking = noticing). It sits a few paragraphs after literal chalk marking and while Havel chalks routes, so a reader can briefly take it as a physical mark. The literal uses carry the plot and cannot go. Under the guide's rule to keep literal uses over metaphorical ones, the mental use is the instance to cut. The verb count alone (2) is at the cap, so this is a density and ambiguity call, graded MILD.
findings.suggestedFix: She went on down Hurdle Lane at his side and looked once more down Tenter Row to the bend as she passed it.
findings.fixNote: Drop-in replacement for the whole sentence. Sylvanas stays the agent and the mental 'marking' becomes a plain tactical look. She was already looking down the row at L243 ('where she was looking'), so 'once more' is accurate. 'as she passed it' now refers to Tenter Row, whose mouth she actually passes; she never passes the bend itself. The fix adds no new observation, and the later payoff ('She had seen it over the bend in Tenter Row', L307) still lands.
